supportedTransactions.quote: The following transactions are supported for the MasterCard fleet card:

entryModes.quote: The default track that is sent to BUYPASS on an original transaction should be Track 2.
If the device cannot read Track 2, then the device should send unaltered Track 1 before attempting manual entry.
Manual entry is allowed on MasterCard fleet card transactions.
Card data provided in a follow-on transaction must be partial Track 2 Data.

exclusions: MasterCard Enhanced Fleet EMV (ATL105 Product IDs MCF and MGF) is a distinct program; see reconciliation MCF-R13.
Generic Mastercard credit purchases do not inherit any rule in this context.
Petroleum Appendix A is limited to its MasterCard Fleet row and Appendix B to product codes; other card rows belong to later contexts.
Cross-card AFP, transaction and receipt chapters 2 to 4 belong to a later context.

inventory.quote: This chapter discusses the following topics related to MasterCard fleet card processing:
This section discusses the following processing requirements for the MasterCard fleet card:
The following transactions are supported for the MasterCard fleet card:
the transaction is processed and sent to BUYPASS as a regular MasterCard transaction using Prompt Code 20.
the Merchant Profile at BUYPASS must have Terminal Special Code 034 enabled.
The POS application must be able to read the Card Type code 080 sent in the Table Load response.
Please refer to the applicable message format specifications for information about valid Prompt Codes for the MasterCard fleet card.
If it is required, the Driver ID can have a length of 1–6 digits. It should be unencrypted in the message format for BUYPASS.
it should prompt the user to swipe the card again—up to three times.
all six digits of the embossed 6-digit ISO Number and all ten digits of the embossed 10-digit Personal Account Number must be entered.
The device must perform an expiration date validation on all MasterCard fleet card transactions.
The MasterCard fleet card expiration date is suppressed on the cardholder’s copy of the receipt.
Note: For all authorizations, merchants must send a value even for expired cards.
For MasterCard fleet cards, a Mod 10 Check Digit evaluation is performed on the full Account Number.
If it is required, the odometer reading can have a length of 1–8 digits.
If it is required, the Vehicle Number can have a length of 1–6 digits.
The device must perform an interrogation on the Product Restriction Code
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchase.
The Product Code Data must be sent in all fleet transactions. The sum of all the products in the product segment must equal the total transaction amount.
The default track that is sent to BUYPASS on an original transaction should be Track 2.
Card data provided in a follow-on transaction must be partial Track 2 Data.

reconciliation.topic: Fallback to regular MasterCard processing with Prompt Code 20
reconciliation.note: In ATL105, 020 is the generic Credit card type; a full Prompt Code combines a transaction type with a card type. The exact four-character fleet and fallback Prompt Codes per transaction remain unconfirmed.

reconciliation.topic: Follow-on card data is partial Track 2 (account number, equals sign, YYMM expiry)
reconciliation.note: Petroleum says follow-on transaction; ATL105 describes the scenario for previously authorized credit transactions. Confirm both terms cover the same transactions.
reconciliation.question: Confirm that Petroleum follow-on transactions match the ATL105 transactions that must carry only account number and expiration date.

reconciliation.topic: Device expiration validation on every MasterCard fleet transaction
reconciliation.note: ATL105 requires island devices or controllers to verify expiration data when applicable; Petroleum makes it mandatory for all MasterCard fleet transactions. Expiry validation must stay separate from the rule to transmit expired-card values (MCF-R06).
reconciliation.question: Confirm the expected device or host outcome when expiry validation fails, given that authorizations still transmit expired-card values.

reconciliation.topic: Product sum equals the total transaction amount
reconciliation.note: ATL105 Element 41 nets discounts and coupons from fuel product amounts. The Petroleum equality rule needs a defined treatment of discounts, coupons, taxes and rounding.
reconciliation.question: Define how discounts, coupons, taxes and rounding affect the product-sum equality (links PETRO-Q002).

atl105.quote: this amount is the net amount derived by subtracting the discount and/or coupon amount from the sum of fuel products in Product Amount (No. 76).

reconciliation.question: Confirm whether any Enhanced Fleet EMV rule also applies to Petroleum chapter 7 MasterCard fleet transactions.

reconciliation.topic: Odometer maximum: 7 digits in Appendix A versus 8 in chapter 7 and ATL105
reconciliation.note: Chapter 7.1.7 and ATL105 Element 64 allow 1 to 8 digits; the Appendix A MasterCard Fleet row says a maximum of 7. Drafts accept 8 digits and flag that oracle as conflicting.
reconciliation.question: Which maximum controls MasterCard fleet odometer prompts: 7 digits (Appendix A) or 8 digits (chapter 7 and ATL105 Element 64)?

reconciliation.topic: Product Restriction Code values other than 1 and 2
reconciliation.note: The track layouts list only values 1 and 2; Appendix A allows all products for any value other than 2. Drafts reject other values and flag that oracle as conflicting.
reconciliation.question: Should a Product Restriction Code other than 1 or 2 be rejected as invalid track data or treated as all products allowed?

reconciliation.topic: Prompts by Product Type Code and keyed entry
reconciliation.note: Appendix A confirms Driver ID for type 3, Vehicle Number for type 2, ID for type 1 (each up to 6 digits) and, when keyed, prompts for ID and Odometer only, matching chapter 7.
reconciliation.question: Confirm that the Appendix A 'ID No.' prompt is carried in ATL105 Element 31 Driver/Identification Number.
